title: Keep train sequences strictly linear; model new paths as new trains

facts.note: Train spec files are identifiable by path/file kind in the plan tree.
Planner is creating a train or changing any train's sequence (including ordinary linear sequences).
Task wording that involves train sequence design.

values: sequence element other than a step added
facts.note: Requires a diff-level parser of the train sequence to detect any sequence change, loop/route elements, numbering gaps, and from/to cardinality.

Whether a planned flow introduces a loop/route construct, branching, or a new/alternative path (which must become a new train) is a design judgement. Steps written out explicitly one after another in a linear sequence are not by themselves a finding; only loop/route elements or branching are.

fires: Planner authors a new train, including an ordinary linear step sequence (numbering and from/to cardinality still apply)
Planner creates a new train to carry an alternative path split out of another train
Planner inserts, removes or reorders steps in an existing train
Planner adds a loop or route element to a train sequence
Planner models an alternative/error path inside an existing train instead of a new train
Train steps are renumbered leaving a gap (e.g. step 1, 2, 4)
A step declares more than one from or more than one to, or omits one
doesNotFire: Editing train metadata outside the sequence (title, description) without touching steps
Planning artifacts that are not trains (wagons, WMBTs, acceptances) with no train sequence change

when: you author or change any train sequence (e.g. adding steps, or when the flow seems to need a loop, a route, a branch or an alternative path)
then: Keep the train's sequence strictly linear (steps only, no loops, routes or branching) and express every new path as a new train.
prefer: Model each new or alternative path as its own new linear train instead of a loop, route or branch inside the existing sequence
Number steps sequentially with no gaps (1, 2, 3, …)
Give every step exactly one from and exactly one to
avoid: Adding loop or route sequence elements to a train
Encoding branching through a step with multiple from/to targets
Leaving gaps in step numbering after inserting or removing steps
why: Linearity is the no-loops/no-routes/no-branching rule for train sequences: sequences contain steps only, and new paths MUST become new trains rather than variations inside one sequence.
evidence: The train sequence contains only step elements — no loop or route elements
Step numbers are contiguous with no gaps
Each step has exactly one from and exactly one to
Any new or alternative path introduced by the plan exists as its own new train
verifier_detail: Enforcement: loop and route sequence elements are forbidden; sequential step numbering must have no gaps; each step has exactly one from and one to.
Constraint: loop and route sequence elements are forbidden
Constraint: sequential step numbering must have no gaps
Constraint: each step has exactly one from and one to
Term 'linearity': the no-loops/no-routes/no-branching rule for train sequences.
